journal:
I recall him telling me this was his fifth expedition to the Andean cloud forests in as many years, after over two decades of research and groundwork, he'd finally managed to track down what he believed to be irrefutable proof of the existance of a new ancient civilisation.

I was told that on his second expedition in peru he was able to get a local translator to speak to the tribes living at the base of a cloud forest, apparently they spoke of an ancient giant that lay slumbering under canopy some 20 miles into the range, of course he didn't have the supplies or the local knowledge to attempt such a dangerous journey, so a year later he came back with two translators, and enough supplies for a dozen men to journey out there, unfortunately luck never seemed on their side.

Every expedition he got closer and closer to the destination, by the time I joined him were were thirty strong, and he had managed to procure ten llamas to help carry supplies. Eventually after three weeks of cutting through the dense jungle brush we came upon a clearing hidden away in a shallow valley.

I remember the moment he must have seen it, everyone was ordered to stop in their tracks, then I was called forward from the back of the caravan and told to bring my sketching implements. "Take as long as you need, but please capture as many details as you can, this may be the first and last time we ever look upon its face".
prompt: Low in the ferns at the edge of a forest clearing, a single shaft of moonlight falls on the moss-covered face of an ancient stone golem.

music.why: A moonlit ancient stone giant discovered after years of jungle expeditions calls for awed, reverent discovery music with an adventurous film-score scale.
